paragraphs.text: Skeleton placeholder. Research CHFA Round One and Round Two Housing Tax Credit award announcements (2022-2026) for any Town of Crested Butte project awards or denials. Verify against the CHFA awards index at chfainfo.com/rental-housing/housing-credit/awards and the per-round narrative PDFs.

Skeleton placeholder. Research the housing fund, dedicated revenue streams (lodging / STR / sales tax / mill levy), recent housing-strategic-plan adoptions, inclusionary ordinances, fee waivers, and council resolutions specific to Town of Crested Butte.

Skeleton placeholder. Identify the public housing authority serving Town of Crested Butte (municipal, county, or regional) plus any coalition memberships (e.g. WMRHC, CHA, APCHA, etc.). Document the authority's voucher inventory and any project-based vouchers committed to local LIHTC pipeline.

The Affordable Ownership Need screening module recommends Ownership-supportive strategy for Town of Crested Butte. It classifies rental pressure as Moderate, ownership pressure as High, and identifies 117 moderate-income renter households as the ownership-fit base.

The same screening run counts 76 renter households and 119 owner households as cost-burdened. This is a screening estimate only; verify local prices, financing assumptions, assistance programs, household size, and local deed-restriction policy before using it for a project decision.

Adopted plans. Crested Butte 5-Year Housing Strategy (adopted May 18, 2026): Targets lower income renters (at or below 60% AMI), middle income homebuyers (at or below 120% AMI) and supportive housing; strategies to produce and steward deed-restricted housing.

Incentives and local funding on record: waived system development fees; waived building permit fees; and lodging or short-term-rental tax. The Local Housing Incentives page has the terms and sources of each.

Council and planning commission record. On January 20, 2026, the Town Council approved: Ordinance No. 1, Series 2026 authorizing sale of deed-restricted unit 828 Gothic Avenue #1A with new income and asset limits. Town bought the deed-restricted unit to add income and asset limits to the deed restriction and resell it by lottery under the Affordable Housing Guidelines. On June 15, 2026, the Town Council approved: Resolution No. 13, Series 2026 approving the 2026 Amended Affordable Housing Guidelines. Amended guidelines govern eligibility, income qualification and lotteries for the Town's deed-restricted affordable housing.

In the Opportunity Finder this record adds a local support bonus of +6 of a possible +6 points as of October 10, 2026: plans +2, incentives and funding +2, council and planning commission +2. A part with nothing counted adds nothing; it never lowers the score.

The metric digest ranks Town of Crested Butte at #193 with an overall housing-need score of 53.6. It identifies 68 deeply affordable units missing at <=30% AMI. The deep-affordability gap rate is 100% of <=30% AMI households. 53.8% of renter households are cost burdened, and 0% of occupied households are overcrowded.
Market and supply context: the digest reports a ZHVI market estimate of $1,481,036 and median gross rent of $1,365. 31.6% of households rent, and 4.7% of the housing stock is multifamily.

Demographics and demand: the population metric is 1,229. LEHD-based commuting signals show 1,682 in-commuters and a commute ratio of 87.7%. The digest's county-context projection shows 120 future units needed over 20 years, so that projection should be read as county context rather than a place trend.
Opportunity context: the digest gives an opportunity score of 43.2 and a walkability score of 57.5. These are current digest levels, not trends.

Economic and service-worker context: the digest reports a workforce-housing pressure score of 81.8. A worker earning the containing county's LEHD earnings-bin wage estimate faces an ownership affordability gap of $333,573 and a rent affordability gap of $27,100. The county-context service-sector employment share is 35.6%, and county-context ACS cohorts show median gross rent changed 90.5% from 2009 to 2024 while median household income changed 47.1%. These county-context figures are economic context, not place-level sector or wage observations.
